title: Script
description: Top-level Script document as edited in script-studio and executed by ScriptEngine.

interfaceVersion.description: Schema/feature version of this script. Version 21 introduces the flat `assets/` folder, the per-action `actionAssets[]` registry, and the `tmp/` runtime folder (renamed from `scriptAssets/`). Readers branch on this value; older scripts use the nested `actions/N-row/M-{actionName}/assets/...` layout.

shortDescription.description: One to three lines: what the script does and when to run it. Shown to agents in list_scripts, so they can pick a script without reading it.

description.description: The longer account an agent reads before running the script: the state it expects to start from, the steps it takes from there, and the state it leaves the device in.

scriptReference.description: Embedded scriptReference props for nested scripts. TODO: tighten once ScriptReference shape is stable.

actionGroupCounter.description: Interface version 22+: the next actionGroup to allocate. Never goes down, so a deleted action's id is never reused (VERSIONING.md §4.7). Absent before v22.

rowIDCounter.description: Interface version 22+: the next rowID to allocate. Never goes down (VERSIONING.md §4.7). Absent before v22.

app.description: Optional: which app the script drives, as its author names it (e.g. "WAO"). Scripts with the same app share one UI graph in their workspace (UI_MAPPER.md §2). Absent or empty: the mapper infers the app. A label, not an identifier: matched after trimming, ignoring case.

AgentToolManifest.description: props.agentTool, present when the script is served to agents as a typed tool: how an agent calls it as an MCP tool. Its name, what it does, its typed inputs and outputs, and what it does to the device. Secrets and user prompts are not declared here: the server derives them from the script's call tree. Versioned with the script, so approving a version approves its manifest too, and the semantic merge treats it as one value.

name.description: The MCP tool name within its toolkit. Absent, the server derives snake_case from the script name minus its {Area}_ prefix (VDI_OpenApp becomes open_app).

description.description: What the tool does, written for the agent that chooses it: the tool description it is served with.

inputs.description: The tool's parameters: one JSON Schema per entry of the script's inputs.json, keyed by the same name. A name the script lacks, or a missing required input, fails validation when the script is merged.

outputs.description: What a call returns: one JSON Schema per entry of the script's outputs.json, keyed by the same name.

effects.description: reads-device: it only looks (screens, OCR) and types nothing into an app. changes-device: anything else. Clients that tell read-only tools apart get it as the MCP readOnlyHint annotation.

repeatable.description: Calling the tool twice with the same inputs is safe. Served as the MCP idempotentHint annotation.

precondition.description: Informational: the name of the script the tool calls first, such as the one that makes sure a session is open. The toolkit guide can mention it; the tool calls it itself either way.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long a call waits for the script's run to finish.

okOutput.description: The output that says whether the call did what it is for, such as ok, ready or opened: true is an ok outcome, anything else a failed one. A member must have one to be promoted from a protocol step to a typed tool (docs/agent-toolkits-plan.md §14.4). It must name an output of outputs and of outputs.json, of type boolean.

AgentToolValueSchema.description: A JSON Schema for one input or output value, such as { "type": "string", "description": "…" }. Any JSON Schema keyword is allowed.
